name: Wireless Optical Communication
description: Introduction to wireless optical communication: motivation, advantages and limitations, and comparison with RF systems. Optical beams: Gaussian, Laguerre–Gaussian and vector beams; beam expanders and collimators; Kolmogorov turbulence model; beam wandering, spreading, and scintillation; statistical turbulence models such as log-normal and gamma-gamma distributions; weather effects including fog, rain, and dust. Optical sources and detectors: LEDs, semiconductor lasers, photodiodes; noise characteristics; optical modulators and filters. Modulation and coding: intensity modulation with direct detection, on–off keying, pulse position modulation; BER, capacity and outage analysis under turbulence. Link budget and system design: eye-safety standards, received power, geometric losses, receiver sensitivity, aperture averaging, spatial diversity, and system design trade-offs. Mitigation techniques: diversity methods, adaptive optics, channel coding, hybrid links, and beam engineering.
